mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES stays depressed and RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday discretionary trips remain substituted by home-based routines, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior 4 weeks while WORKPLACES remains below baseline and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline for the full next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week pickup in GROCERY_PHARM above recent levels reflects more errand activity and higher local trip chaining, which spills into retail visits and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 3 points and stays above that level for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 2 weeks after GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 3 points for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT continues to edge up while WORKPLACES stays flat or lower, more commuting traffic reaches shopping corridors without a corresponding office recovery, producing a modest rise in RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for 3 consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES does not increase by at least 1 point over the same span
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks despite sustained transit gains and no meaningful workplace recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility competes with indoor shopping time and shifts leisure demand away from retail and recreation, so RETAIL_REC weakens over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 4 weeks while PARKS continues to rise or remains above its prior 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops sharply, it signals a mobility restriction or service shock that directly suppresses shopping access, causing RETAIL_REC to fall within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by 2 points or more week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after a TRANSIT drop of at least 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates household errand-and-leisure substitution toward local nonretail trips, which reduces discretionary retail visits over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks while both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are above their last-4-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES keeps edging lower from an already weak level, the loss of commute-linked purchases outweighs stable residential presence and keeps RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below its prior 4-week average by at least 1 point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below the prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES slips below its 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: During a reopening regime, a persistent reduction in RESIDENTIAL time combined with stable or rising TRANSIT marks more out-of-home activity, which should lift retail and recreation mobility over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 4 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining near or below its current level and TRANSIT not weakening.
